---
title: "How do I plot paired numeric variables and show a fitted line?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I plot paired numeric variables and show a fitted line?

## Steps to decide and solve

Identify paired x and y measurements from the same rows; plot and label both axes; add a line only after inspecting curves and unusual points.

## Worked example: cars

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("cars")
fit <- ru_apply("scatterplot", data=d, x="speed", y="dist")
stopifnot(inherits(fit,"lm"))
```

Speed and stopping distance are measured on different scales and show an association in the recorded cars. The fitted straight line summarizes a relationship; it does not establish causation or work equally well at unobserved speeds.

## Apply it to another question

```r
ru_apply("scatterplot", data=your_data, x="predictor", y="response")
```

When the pattern is curved, compare a nonlinear model or descriptive smoothing before interpreting a Pearson coefficient.

## Optional Palmer penguins example

```r
if (requireNamespace("palmerpenguins", quietly=TRUE)) {
  penguins <- ru_data("penguins")
  ru_apply("scatterplot", data=penguins,
           x="bill_length_mm", y="bill_depth_mm")
}
```

Use `ru_plan("scatterplot")` to inspect alternative routes when required information is absent or uncertain.
